dataset_title: Fitted ADM1 disintegration and hydrolysis rates for grass silage
publisher: Carl von Ossietzky University of Oldenburg repository (dissertation); Bioresource Technology (article)
article_title: Application of Anaerobic Digestion Model No. 1 for describing anaerobic digestion of grass, maize, green weed silage, and industrial glycerine

numeric_table_source.title: Model based sustainable production of biomethane
numeric_table_source.author: Piotr Biernacki

geography: Germany; grass silage associated with the EWE Wittmund biogas power plant study
material_scope: Grass silage, not fresh roadside grass, screw-pressed cake, protein-extraction residual, or GreenHub-specific substrate.

methods.model: ADM1 with Wett et al. modification
methods.parameter_estimation: Downhill simplex (Nelder-Mead) optimization against cumulative batch biogas production
methods.replicates: Three parallel bottles per substrate; experiment repeated

uncertainty: The table gives no confidence intervals or parameter covariance. The dissertation notes that multiple kinetic-constant sets can fit the data; this does not establish transferability to a different substrate.
processing: Transcribed the four grass-silage fitted constants from Table 17, p.102. Converted d^-1 to s^-1 by dividing by 86,400; original reported values are retained. No curves were digitized and no refit was performed.
license: No explicit reuse license identified for the dissertation or article; only four factual numeric parameter estimates are transcribed with attribution.
limitations: These are model-fitted estimates, not direct measurements of rate constants.
The calibration substrate is grass silage and differs from GreenHub fresh roadside grass, press cake and isoelectric-process residuals.
Do not use as a GreenHub default or parameter-registry value without route-specific validation against time-series BMP and reactor data.
The fitted values are conditional on the modified ADM1 structure, substrate characterization, 38 C batch protocol and estimation method.
No uncertainty interval or parameter covariance was reported in the table; do not invent one.
